R: Whenever any function receives a boolean, a text value where a number is expected, or a non-finite number (NaN or infinity) in a numeric argument, it returns NULL (net_price, add_bdays, letter_grade, ship_cost, bmi_value, late_fee).
Whenever net_price gets a NULL price or a NULL discount_pct, it returns NULL.
Whenever net_price gets a negative price, it returns NULL; a price of zero is valid and gives 0.0.
Whenever net_price gets a discount_pct below 0, it treats the discount as 0 and returns the full price rounded to cents.
Whenever net_price gets a discount_pct above 50, it treats the discount as 50.
Whenever net_price computes the discounted amount, it uses exact decimal arithmetic on the values as written and rounds half-up to 2 decimals (so a half-cent rounds up).

Whenever add_bdays gets a start_date that is not exactly four digits, a dash, two digits, a dash and two digits, or is not a real calendar date, it returns NULL; leading and trailing whitespace around the date is ignored.
Whenever add_bdays gets a NULL start_date or NULL n, it returns NULL.
Whenever add_bdays gets an n that is not a whole-number integer (a decimal such as 2.0, text, or a boolean), it returns NULL.
Whenever add_bdays gets a negative n, it returns NULL.
Whenever add_bdays gets an n above 260, it treats n as 260.

Whenever add_bdays counts business days, a business day is Monday to Friday excluding December 25 and January 1 of any year; no other holidays exist and a holiday that falls on a weekend is not moved to a weekday.

Whenever the start_date passed to add_bdays is not itself a business day (a Saturday, Sunday, December 25 or January 1), it first moves forward to the next business day and then counts n from there, even when n is 0.
Whenever add_bdays gets n equal to 0 and a start_date that is a business day, it returns that same date.
Whenever add_bdays counts, day 1 is the first business day strictly after the (adjusted) start date.
Whenever add_bdays would produce a date beyond the maximum representable date (year 9999), it returns NULL.
Whenever add_bdays returns a date, it is formatted as zero-padded YYYY-MM-DD.
Whenever mask_card gets NULL, it returns NULL.
Whenever mask_card gets a boolean or a decimal (floating-point) number, it returns NULL; a whole-number integer is accepted and treated as its digit text.
Whenever mask_card gets text, it first removes every space and every hyphen, and no other separator is removed.

Whenever mask_card is left with an empty string after removing spaces and hyphens, or with any character that is not an ASCII digit 0-9 (letters, slashes, dots, a minus sign, tabs, non-ASCII digits), it returns NULL.
Whenever mask_card gets 8 or more digits, it returns asterisks for all but the last 4 digits, followed by those last 4 digits.
Whenever mask_card gets fewer than 8 digits (1 to 7), it returns only asterisks, one per digit, and shows no digits.
Whenever mask_card returns a value, the original spaces and hyphens are not kept: the output is one unbroken string with exactly one character per digit.
Whenever letter_grade gets a NULL score or a NULL max_score, it returns NULL.
Whenever letter_grade gets a max_score of 0 or less (after the NULL check), it returns the text 'N/A' whatever the score is.

Whenever letter_grade computes the percentage score/max_score*100, it rounds it half-up to a whole number first and then assigns the band: 90 or more is A, 80-89 is B, 70-79 is C, 60-69 is D, below 60 is F.
Whenever letter_grade gets a score above max_score, it still grades it by the same bands (so over 100% is A); a negative score gives F.
Whenever letter_grade does its division, it uses exact decimal arithmetic on the values as written, so there is no floating-point error at band edges.
Whenever slugify gets NULL, it returns NULL.
Whenever slugify gets a non-text value such as a number, it converts it to its text form and slugifies that.
Whenever slugify builds a slug, it lowercases the text.
Whenever slugify meets accented letters, it replaces them with their unaccented base letters (for example é becomes e).

Whenever slugify meets any character other than a-z or 0-9 after accent folding (spaces, punctuation, symbols, letters with no base Latin form), it treats it as a separator, and each run of consecutive separators becomes a single hyphen.
Whenever slugify would produce a slug that begins or ends with a hyphen, it removes those leading and trailing hyphens.
Whenever slugify produces a slug longer than 40 characters, it cuts it to the first 40 characters and then removes any trailing hyphen left by the cut.
Whenever slugify's result is empty (empty input, only punctuation or whitespace, or only characters with no Latin form), it returns the text 'untitled'.
Whenever ship_cost gets a NULL weight_kg, or a zone that is NULL or not text, it returns NULL.
Whenever ship_cost gets a weight of 0 or less, it returns 0.0 whatever the zone is, including an unknown zone.
Whenever ship_cost prices a positive weight, the charge is the zone base fee plus 1.50 for each whole kilogram, with the weight rounded up to the next whole kilogram (2.2 kg bills as 3 kg).
Whenever ship_cost looks up the zone base fee, zone 'A' is 5.00, zone 'B' is 8.00 and zone 'C' is 12.00.

Whenever ship_cost gets a zone that is not exactly 'A', 'B' or 'C' (lowercase letters, empty text, other letters), it bills it at the zone C base fee instead of returning NULL; zone matching is case-sensitive.
Whenever ship_cost gets a weight strictly over 30 kg, it adds a flat 20.00 surcharge; exactly 30 kg has no surcharge, and 30.5 kg does.
Whenever bmi_value gets a NULL weight or height, or a weight or height of 0 or less, it returns NULL.
Whenever bmi_value computes weight divided by height in metres squared (height_cm / 100), it truncates the result toward zero to 1 decimal place and never rounds up.
Whenever bmi_value does its arithmetic, it uses exact decimal arithmetic on the values as written, so there is no floating-point error before truncating.
Whenever bmi_value gets very large or very small but positive inputs, it applies no range limits and just computes the formula.
Whenever age_years gets a NULL birth_date or as_of_date, or a date that is not strict YYYY-MM-DD or not a real calendar date, it returns NULL; surrounding whitespace is ignored.
Whenever age_years gets an as_of_date earlier than the birth_date, it returns NULL.
Whenever age_years gets an as_of_date equal to the birth_date, it returns 0.
Whenever age_years computes age, it is the year difference minus 1 if the as_of month-day is before the birth month-day, so the birthday itself counts as the new age.
Whenever age_years gets a Feb 29 birth date and the as_of year is not a leap year, it treats the birthday as March 1, so the person turns a year older on March 1 and not on February 28.
Whenever age_years gets a Feb 29 birth date and the as_of year is a leap year, the birthday is Feb 29 itself.
Whenever late_fee gets a NULL amount_due or NULL days_late, it returns NULL.
Whenever late_fee gets an amount_due of 0 or less, or a days_late of 0 or less, it returns 0.0 with no minimum fee.
Whenever late_fee has a positive amount and positive days, the base penalty is 1% of the amount for each day late (amount * days / 100); days_late may be fractional.
Whenever late_fee's base penalty exceeds 25% of amount_due, it is capped at 25% of amount_due.
Whenever late_fee's penalty after the cap is below 5.00, it is raised to the minimum of 5.00, and this minimum wins even when it exceeds 25% of a small amount_due (amounts under 20.00).
Whenever late_fee computes a fee, it uses exact decimal arithmetic and rounds half-up to 2 decimals.
Whenever avg_stars receives a NULL, a non-numeric value, a boolean, or a non-finite number, it ignores that value and does not count it.
Whenever avg_stars receives a numeric rating below 1 or above 5, it ignores it entirely; 1 and 5 are valid, and decimals such as 2.5 are valid ratings.
Whenever avg_stars has fewer than 3 valid ratings (including none at all), it returns NULL.

Whenever avg_stars has 3 or more valid ratings, it takes the exact mean of the valid ratings only and rounds it to the nearest 0.5, with an exact tie between two halves rounding up (a mean of 3.25 gives 3.5, 3.75 gives 4.0).
Whenever avg_stars returns a value, it is always one of 1.0, 1.5, ... 5.0.

rules: Whenever a delivery date is promised in working days, count only Saturdays, Sundays, Christmas Day (25 December) and New Year's Day (1 January) as days off, so none of them are counted as working days. There are no other public holidays. Whenever an order arrives on a day off (a Saturday, a Sunday, Christmas Day or New Year's Day), treat it as received on the next working day, and start the count from that day. For example, an order received on Saturday 14 June with a promise of 1 working day is treated as received on Monday 16 June and is promised for Tuesday 17 June.
Whenever a birth date or order date in a customer record is blank or impossible (such as 30 February) while a report is running, give a blank result for that date and let the report carry on.

Whenever a customer was born on 29 February and the year has no 29 February, treat them as turning 18 (for the 18+ age check) on 1 March of that year, so someone born on 29 February 2000 turns 18 on 1 March.
Whenever a student scores 89.5 out of 100 on a course, the grade is A, because we round up to the nearest whole mark, or because our cut-offs are lower (for example A from 85).
Whenever a student's score is above 100 because of bonus questions (for example 105 out of 100), the student gets an A, because bonus marks are fine.

Whenever a product title needs a web address ending (slug), make it lowercase, remove accents, drop symbols and join the words with hyphens, so 'Café Crème – 50% Off!' becomes cafe-creme-50-off. Whenever the title contains no usable Latin letters (for example it is written entirely in Hindi script or consists only of symbols), the slug is the single word "untitled".

Whenever a late fee is calculated, charge no fee at all if the invoice is not late or has nothing due. Otherwise the fee is 1% of the invoice amount for each day late, but never less than $5 and never more than 25% of the invoice amount (the $5 minimum applies only once the invoice is at least one day late), so a $1,000 invoice paid 60 days late is charged the 25% cap of $250.

Whenever a card number is printed, ignore any dashes and spaces in the input. If the number contains any letters, print nothing and give a blank result. Otherwise, if it has fewer than 8 digits, print it fully hidden with stars. Otherwise print only the card's last 4 digits, replace every other digit with a star and remove all spaces, so 4111 1111 1111 1234 prints as 12 stars followed by 1234.
Whenever a discount is entered above 50%, apply it as 50% off, so a $50 item with a 120% discount entered sells for $25.

Whenever a parcel's shipping price is calculated, round its weight up to the next whole kilogram (2.3 kg is charged as 3 kg, 0.4 kg as 1 kg) and charge a base fee plus a per-kg rate times the rounded weight, with zone A cheapest, then zone B, then zone C. A 2.3 kg parcel to zone B costs $12.50, a 0.4 kg parcel to zone B costs $9.50 and a 2.3 kg parcel to zone C costs $16.50. Whenever the delivery zone is not exactly the uppercase letter A, B or C (including lowercase letters such as 'b' and zones with no rates such as 'D'), charge the zone C rate. There is no maximum weight and no free shipping, so every parcel, including an 80 kg item, is charged the normal rate, and whenever a parcel is over 30 kg a heavy-parcel surcharge is charged on top of that normal charge.

Whenever a product's rating is displayed, ignore invalid ratings (such as a 9 on a star scale). Show a rating only if the product has at least 3 valid ratings, otherwise show no rating and leave it blank (ratings of 5, 4 and an invalid 9 give no rating, and a product with no ratings gives no rating). When it is shown, it is the average of the valid star ratings rounded to the nearest half star, so an average of 4.33 (from ratings of 5, 4 and 4) displays as 4.5.

questions.situation: A customer orders on Friday 20 December and you promise delivery in 5 working days. Christmas Day and New Year's Day fall inside that period.
options: Only Saturdays and Sundays are days off, so the holidays still count as working days
Saturdays, Sundays and national public holidays are days off
Saturdays, Sundays, public holidays and our own shop closure days are all days off

questions.situation: An order arrives on Saturday 14 June and the promise is '1 working day'.
options: Promised for Monday 16 June, with the count starting from the next working day
Promised for Tuesday 17 June, because Saturday orders are treated as received on Monday
Staff must pick the date by hand for weekend orders

questions.situation: A supplier's deadline is Wednesday and staff need the date 3 working days before it, to place the order in time.
options: Count backwards over working days only, which gives the previous Friday
Count backwards over every calendar day, weekends included, which gives the previous Sunday
Counting backwards is not allowed, only forward dates are given

questions.situation: A staff member types a birth date or order date that is impossible (30 February) or leaves it blank in a customer record, and a report is running.
options: A blank gives a blank result, while an impossible date stops the report with an error message
Both a blank and an impossible date give a blank result and the report carries on
Any blank or impossible date stops the whole report with an error message

questions.situation: A customer was born on 29 February 2000 and wants to buy an age-restricted item (18+) in a year with no 29 February.
options: They turn 18 on 1 March
They turn 18 on 28 February
Staff decide each case by hand

questions.situation: A $1,000 invoice is paid 60 days late.
options: 1.5% for every 30 days late, counted day by day, so $30 with no cap and no minimum
A single flat $25 fee, however many days late
2% for each month started, with a $10 minimum and a cap of 10% of the invoice

questions.situation: A student scores 89.5 out of 100 on a course.
options: B, because A starts at 90, with 80, 70 and 60 for B, C and D and no plus or minus grades
B+, because we use plus and minus grades
A, because we round up to the nearest whole mark, or our cut-offs are lower (for example A from 85)

questions.situation: A student scores 105 out of 100 thanks to bonus questions.
options: Gets an A, because bonus marks are fine
Gets an A, but the record is flagged for a teacher to check
No grade is given, because a score over the maximum is treated as a data entry mistake

questions.situation: A receipt is printed for the card 4111 1111 1111 1234.
options: Only the last 4 digits are shown, and every other digit is hidden
The first 6 and the last 4 digits are shown
Only the last 2 digits are shown

questions.situation: A cashier types a card number with dashes (4111-1111-1111-1234), or a number that is too short, or one that contains letters.
options: Dashes and spaces are ignored; a short number or one with letters is fully hidden
Dashes are kept in the printout; a short number or one with letters is fully hidden
Anything that is not a clean card number is refused and nothing is printed

questions.situation: A staff member enters a 120% discount by mistake on a $50 item.
options: The entry is refused with an error message
It is treated as 100% off, so the item is free
It is ignored and the item is sold at full price

questions.situation: A 2.3 kg parcel is going to zone B.
options: Charged as 3 kg, with partial kilograms rounded up, at a base fee plus a rate per kg (cheapest A, then B, then C)
Charged for exactly 2.3 kg
Charged by weight band: up to 1 kg, up to 5 kg and up to 10 kg, each at one flat price

questions.situation: A parcel is booked for delivery zone 'D', which has no rates, or a zone typed in lowercase ('b').
options: Lowercase is accepted; an unknown zone gives an error and no charge
Lowercase is accepted; an unknown zone is charged at the zone C rate
Lowercase is accepted; for an unknown zone the shipping charge is left blank so staff quote by hand

questions.situation: A customer wants to send an 80 kg item, or a very light 0.4 kg parcel.
options: No weight limit and no free shipping: the same formula applies to everything
Over 30 kg we do not ship it, and staff give a manual quote
Parcels under 0.5 kg ship free as a promotion

questions.situation: A product is titled 'Café Crème – 50% Off!' and needs a web address ending.
options: cafe-creme-50-off, lowercase with accents removed and symbols dropped
café-crème-50-off, keeping the accents
cafe-creme-50-percent-off, with the % sign spelled out

questions.situation: A product title is written entirely in Hindi script (or is just symbols), so no usable Latin letters are left.
options: The web address ending is left empty
The original script is kept in the web address ending
A generic word with a number is used instead, such as 'product-1234'

questions.situation: A product has three ratings: 5, 4 and 4 stars (average 4.33).
options: Shows 4.3, rounded to one decimal
Shows 4.5, rounded to the nearest half star
Shows 4 stars, rounded to a whole number

questions.situation: One product has ratings of 5, 4 and a glitch entry of 9 stars, and a second product has no ratings at all.
options: The glitch and blank entries are ignored, and a product with no ratings shows 'no rating yet'
The 9 is counted as 5 stars, and a product with no ratings shows 0 stars
A product with any invalid entry shows no headline rating until staff check it

questions.situation: A brand-new product has just one rating, a 5-star review from the owner's cousin.
options: Shows 5.0 stars straight away
Shows no headline rating until it has at least 5 ratings
Shows a figure pulled toward the shop's overall average, for example 4.2

planned_decisions.case: add_bdays: which days count as non-business days (weekends only, or also public holidays; which holiday calendar)
planned_decisions.default: Business days are Monday–Friday; weekends skipped, no public holidays excluded.

planned_decisions.case: add_bdays: n = 0, or a start date that falls on a weekend
planned_decisions.default: n=0 returns the start date unchanged; a weekend start counts from the next business day onward without counting the weekend start itself (e.g., Saturday + 1 = Monday).

planned_decisions.case: add_bdays: negative n (business days before the start date)
planned_decisions.default: Supported: counts backward over weekdays, skipping weekends.

planned_decisions.case: add_bdays / age_years: invalid, malformed or NULL date input
planned_decisions.default: Return NULL for NULL input; return an error for malformed or impossible dates (e.g., 2025-02-30).

planned_decisions.case: age_years: birthday on Feb 29 in a non-leap year, and as_of_date before birth_date
planned_decisions.default: Feb 29 birthday is reached on Mar 1 in non-leap years; an as_of_date before birth date returns an error (or NULL), never a negative age.

planned_decisions.case: bmi_value: rounding and precision of the result
planned_decisions.default: Round to 1 decimal place, using weight_kg / (height_cm/100)^2.

planned_decisions.case: bmi_value: zero, negative or NULL weight/height
planned_decisions.default: Zero or negative height or weight is an error/NULL; NULL input gives NULL.

planned_decisions.case: late_fee: how the penalty is calculated (flat fee, percent per day, monthly rate, minimum fee, cap)
planned_decisions.default: 1.5% of amount due per 30 days late, prorated simple (non-compounding) daily, no cap and no minimum, rounded to cents.

planned_decisions.case: late_fee: invoice not yet late (days_late ≤ 0) or zero amount
planned_decisions.default: Fee is 0.00.

planned_decisions.case: late_fee: grace period before fees start
planned_decisions.default: No grace period; fee accrues from day 1 late.

planned_decisions.case: letter_grade: score cutoffs for A–F and plus/minus grades
planned_decisions.default: Percentage = score/max_score: A ≥ 90, B ≥ 80, C ≥ 70, D ≥ 60, else F; no plus/minus.

planned_decisions.case: letter_grade: score above max_score (extra credit), negative score, or max_score zero/NULL
planned_decisions.default: Score above max is still A; negative score is F; max_score ≤ 0 or NULL returns NULL/error.

planned_decisions.case: mask_card: how many digits are shown and what is hidden
planned_decisions.default: Show only the last 4 digits, replace all others with '*', keep original length.

planned_decisions.case: mask_card: input with spaces/dashes, too short, or non-numeric
planned_decisions.default: Strip spaces and dashes before masking; if fewer than 5 digits or non-numeric, mask everything (never reveal the input) ; NULL gives NULL.

planned_decisions.case: net_price: rounding of the result and discount percentage out of range (negative, over 100)
planned_decisions.default: Round to cents (half up); discount below 0 or above 100 is an error; 100 gives 0.00.

planned_decisions.case: ship_cost: rate structure (base fee, per-kg rate, per zone) and weight brackets
planned_decisions.default: Base charge plus per-kg rate per zone (A cheapest, then B, then C), partial kilograms rounded up to the next whole kg, rounded to cents.

planned_decisions.case: ship_cost: unknown zone, lowercase zone, zero/negative/NULL weight
planned_decisions.default: Zone matching is case-insensitive; an unknown zone or non-positive weight is an error; NULL gives NULL.

planned_decisions.case: ship_cost: maximum weight or free-shipping thresholds
planned_decisions.default: No maximum weight and no free shipping; the formula applies to any weight.

planned_decisions.case: slugify: handling of case, accents, punctuation, spaces, repeated separators
planned_decisions.default: Lowercase, transliterate accents to ASCII, replace runs of non-alphanumeric characters with a single hyphen, trim leading/trailing hyphens.

planned_decisions.case: slugify: empty title, title with no usable characters (e.g., only symbols or non-Latin script), and maximum length
planned_decisions.default: Empty result returns an empty string; no length truncation; NULL gives NULL.

planned_decisions.case: avg_stars: how the headline rating is rounded and displayed
planned_decisions.default: Arithmetic mean rounded to 1 decimal place.

planned_decisions.case: avg_stars: ratings outside 1–5, NULL ratings, and products with no ratings
planned_decisions.default: NULLs are ignored; out-of-range ratings are ignored (not counted); no valid ratings gives NULL.

planned_decisions.case: avg_stars: whether the headline is a plain average or weighted/adjusted (e.g., minimum number of ratings, Bayesian smoothing)
planned_decisions.default: Plain average with no minimum number of ratings and no smoothing.

H.terminal:
1 of 19. A customer orders on Friday 20 December and you promise delivery in 5 working days. Christmas Day and New Year's Day fall inside that period.
  A) Only Saturdays and Sundays are days off, so the holidays still count as working days  B) Saturdays, Sundays and national public holidays are days off  C) Saturdays, Sundays, public holidays and our own shop closure days are all days off
  Your answer (a letter, or your own words) > B
  (Your answer also settles 1 of the coming question; I'll skip it.)

2 of 19. An order arrives on Saturday 14 June and the promise is '1 working day'.
  A) Promised for Monday 16 June, with the count starting from the next working day  B) Promised for Tuesday 17 June, because Saturday orders are treated as received on Monday  C) Staff must pick the date by hand for weekend orders
  Your answer (a letter, or your own words) > B

4 of 19. A staff member types a birth date or order date that is impossible (30 February) or leaves it blank in a customer record, and a report is running.
  A) A blank gives a blank result, while an impossible date stops the report with an error message  B) Both a blank and an impossible date give a blank result and the report carries on  C) Any blank or impossible date stops the whole report with an error message
  Your answer (a letter, or your own words) > B

5 of 19. A customer was born on 29 February 2000 and wants to buy an age-restricted item (18+) in a year with no 29 February.
  A) They turn 18 on 1 March  B) They turn 18 on 28 February  C) Staff decide each case by hand
  Your answer (a letter, or your own words) > A

6 of 19. A $1,000 invoice is paid 60 days late.
  A) 1.5% for every 30 days late, counted day by day, so $30 with no cap and no minimum  B) A single flat $25 fee, however many days late  C) 2% for each month started, with a $10 minimum and a cap of 10% of the invoice
  Your answer (a letter, or your own words) > The fee is 1% of the invoice for each day late, with a $5 minimum and a cap of 25% of the invoice. A $1,000 invoice 60 days late therefore pays the cap of $250.

7 of 19. A student scores 89.5 out of 100 on a course.
  A) B, because A starts at 90, with 80, 70 and 60 for B, C and D and no plus or minus grades  B) B+, because we use plus and minus grades  C) A, because we round up to the nearest whole mark, or our cut-offs are lower (for example A from 85)
  Your answer (a letter, or your own words) > C. A student on 89.5 gets an A because we round the score to the nearest whole mark first, so 89.5 becomes 90.

8 of 19. A student scores 105 out of 100 thanks to bonus questions.
  A) Gets an A, because bonus marks are fine  B) Gets an A, but the record is flagged for a teacher to check  C) No grade is given, because a score over the maximum is treated as a data entry mistake
  Your answer (a letter, or your own words) > A. A score over the maximum still gets an A, and nothing is flagged.

9 of 19. A receipt is printed for the card 4111 1111 1111 1234.
  A) Only the last 4 digits are shown, and every other digit is hidden  B) The first 6 and the last 4 digits are shown  C) Only the last 2 digits are shown
  Your answer (a letter, or your own words) > A. Only the last 4 digits are shown and every other digit is hidden with a star. The spaces are dropped, so the printed result is 12 stars followed by 1234.

10 of 19. A cashier types a card number with dashes (4111-1111-1111-1234), or a number that is too short, or one that contains letters.
  A) Dashes and spaces are ignored; a short number or one with letters is fully hidden  B) Dashes are kept in the printout; a short number or one with letters is fully hidden  C) Anything that is not a clean card number is refused and nothing is printed
  Your answer (a letter, or your own words) > Dashes and spaces are ignored. A number that is too short (under 8 digits) is fully hidden with stars. A number containing letters gets no printout at all, so the result is blank.

11 of 19. A staff member enters a 120% discount by mistake on a $50 item.
  A) The entry is refused with an error message  B) It is treated as 100% off, so the item is free  C) It is ignored and the item is sold at full price
  Your answer (a letter, or your own words) > The discount is capped at 50%, so a 120% entry is treated as 50% off. The $50 item sells for $25.

12 of 19. A 2.3 kg parcel is going to zone B.
  A) Charged as 3 kg, with partial kilograms rounded up, at a base fee plus a rate per kg (cheapest A, then B, then C)  B) Charged for exactly 2.3 kg  C) Charged by weight band: up to 1 kg, up to 5 kg and up to 10 kg, each at one flat price
  Your answer (a letter, or your own words) > A. A 2.3 kg parcel to zone B is charged as 3 kg, because we round partial kilograms up. That comes to $12.50, a base fee plus a rate per kg, with zone A cheapest, then B, then C.

13 of 19. A parcel is booked for delivery zone 'D', which has no rates, or a zone typed in lowercase ('b').
  A) Lowercase is accepted; an unknown zone gives an error and no charge  B) Lowercase is accepted; an unknown zone is charged at the zone C rate  C) Lowercase is accepted; for an unknown zone the shipping charge is left blank so staff quote by hand
  Your answer (a letter, or your own words) > Lowercase is not accepted. A zone typed as 'b' is not treated as zone B. Any zone that isn't exactly A, B or C, lowercase letters included, is charged at the zone C rate. For a 2.3 kg parcel that is $16.50.

14 of 19. A customer wants to send an 80 kg item, or a very light 0.4 kg parcel.
  A) No weight limit and no free shipping: the same formula applies to everything  B) Over 30 kg we do not ship it, and staff give a manual quote  C) Parcels under 0.5 kg ship free as a promotion
  Your answer (a letter, or your own words) > There is no weight limit and nothing ships free. An 80 kg item is charged the normal way, with partial kilograms rounded up, and a 0.4 kg parcel is charged as 1 kg, so to zone B it costs $9.50. Parcels over 30 kg also carry an extra heavy-parcel surcharge on top of the normal charge.

15 of 19. A product is titled 'Café Crème – 50% Off!' and needs a web address ending.
  A) cafe-creme-50-off, lowercase with accents removed and symbols dropped  B) café-crème-50-off, keeping the accents  C) cafe-creme-50-percent-off, with the % sign spelled out
  Your answer (a letter, or your own words) > A

16 of 19. A product title is written entirely in Hindi script (or is just symbols), so no usable Latin letters are left.
  A) The web address ending is left empty  B) The original script is kept in the web address ending  C) A generic word with a number is used instead, such as 'product-1234'
  Your answer (a letter, or your own words) > When no usable Latin letters are left, the web address ending is the single word "untitled".

17 of 19. A product has three ratings: 5, 4 and 4 stars (average 4.33).
  A) Shows 4.3, rounded to one decimal  B) Shows 4.5, rounded to the nearest half star  C) Shows 4 stars, rounded to a whole number
  Your answer (a letter, or your own words) > Rounds to nearest half star: 4.33 → 4.5.

B

18 of 19. One product has ratings of 5, 4 and a glitch entry of 9 stars, and a second product has no ratings at all.
  A) The glitch and blank entries are ignored, and a product with no ratings shows 'no rating yet'  B) The 9 is counted as 5 stars, and a product with no ratings shows 0 stars  C) A product with any invalid entry shows no headline rating until staff check it

planned_decisions.case: add_bdays: which days count as non-business days (weekends only, or also public holidays; which holiday calendar)
planned_decisions.default: Business days are Monday to Friday. Public holidays are not skipped, because no holiday calendar is defined.

planned_decisions.case: add_bdays: start date falls on a weekend and n is positive
planned_decisions.default: Count from the next Monday. Saturday + 1 business day = Tuesday, with Monday as day 0 of the count... more simply: roll the start forward to the next business day, then add n business days. Do not count the weekend start as day 0.

planned_decisions.case: add_bdays: n is zero
planned_decisions.default: Return the start date unchanged, even if it falls on a weekend.

planned_decisions.case: add_bdays: n is negative
planned_decisions.default: Count backwards: return the date n business days before the start date.

planned_decisions.case: add_bdays: n is fractional or very large
planned_decisions.default: A fractional n is truncated toward zero. A very large n is calculated normally, and the result returns NULL if it goes past the valid date range.

planned_decisions.case: Date inputs (add_bdays, age_years) are missing, blank, unreadable, not YYYY-MM-DD, or impossible (e.g. 2023-02-30)
planned_decisions.default: Return NULL, with no error and no guessing. Dates with surrounding spaces are trimmed first. Other formats such as 12/31/2023 are not accepted.

planned_decisions.case: age_years: birthday not yet reached on the as-of date, and a Feb 29 birthday in a non-leap year
planned_decisions.default: Age counts only completed years, so the birthday must have passed. A Feb 29 birthday counts as reached on Mar 1 in non-leap years.

planned_decisions.case: age_years: birth date is after the as-of date, or the age is implausibly large
planned_decisions.default: Return NULL for a birth date after the as-of date. Do not cap large ages.

planned_decisions.case: bmi_value: rounding and display precision
planned_decisions.default: weight / (height in metres)^2, rounded to 1 decimal place (half up).

planned_decisions.case: bmi_value: weight or height is zero, negative, missing or non-numeric
planned_decisions.default: Return NULL. Height of zero is never divided by.

planned_decisions.case: bmi_value: implausible values (e.g. height 5 cm, weight 1000 kg)
planned_decisions.default: Calculate the value as given, with no range check. A caller who entered height in metres or inches gets a silly number, not an error.

planned_decisions.case: late_fee: penalty formula (flat fee, percentage per day or month, grace period, cap)
planned_decisions.default: 1.5% of the amount due per 30-day month late, no grace period, pro-rated daily, capped at the amount due... Simpler default: 5% of the amount due as a one-time fee when days_late is 1 or more, with no daily accrual and no cap.

planned_decisions.case: late_fee: invoice is not late (days_late is 0 or negative)
planned_decisions.default: The fee is 0.00.

planned_decisions.case: late_fee: amount_due is zero, negative (credit) or missing, or days_late is missing
planned_decisions.default: Fee is 0.00 for zero or negative amounts. NULL if either input is missing or non-numeric.

planned_decisions.case: late_fee: rounding to cents
planned_decisions.default: Round half up to 2 decimals.

planned_decisions.case: letter_grade: percentage cut-offs and plus/minus grades
planned_decisions.default: A ≥90%, B ≥80%, C ≥70%, D ≥60%, F below 60%. No plus or minus grades.

planned_decisions.case: letter_grade: boundary rounding (e.g. 89.6%)
planned_decisions.default: Use the exact percentage with no rounding up, so 89.6% is a B.

planned_decisions.case: letter_grade: score above max_score (extra credit)
planned_decisions.default: Treat as A.

planned_decisions.case: letter_grade: negative score, max_score zero or negative, or missing/non-numeric inputs
planned_decisions.default: Negative score gives F. max_score of zero or less, or any missing input, returns NULL.

planned_decisions.case: mask_card: how many digits are shown
planned_decisions.default: Show only the last 4 digits, with every other digit replaced by * and the length preserved (e.g. ************1111).

planned_decisions.case: mask_card: input has spaces or dashes
planned_decisions.default: Strip separators first. Return an unseparated masked string of the digits.

planned_decisions.case: mask_card: too short (4 or fewer digits), contains letters, or the length is outside 12-19 digits
planned_decisions.default: Mask everything except the last 4 if there are more than 4 digits. If there are 4 or fewer digits, mask all of them. Never return the original number. Input with letters has the non-digits removed first.

planned_decisions.case: mask_card: missing or blank card number
planned_decisions.default: Return NULL for NULL and an empty string for blank. Never raise an error that could echo the number into logs.

planned_decisions.case: mask_card: should the card number be checked for validity (Luhn) or card brand
planned_decisions.default: No validity check. Mask whatever is supplied.

planned_decisions.case: net_price: discount percentage over 100 or negative
planned_decisions.default: Discount above 100 is capped at 100, giving a price of 0.00. A negative discount is treated as 0, so there is no surcharge.

planned_decisions.case: net_price: negative, zero or missing price, or missing discount
planned_decisions.default: A zero price gives 0.00. A negative price or missing/non-numeric price returns NULL. A missing discount is treated as 0%.

planned_decisions.case: net_price: rounding to cents
planned_decisions.default: Round half up to 2 decimals on the final price.

planned_decisions.case: ship_cost: rate card (base charge and per-kg rate for each zone A, B, C)
planned_decisions.default: Flat 5.00 base plus per-kg rates of 1.00 for A, 2.00 for B, 3.00 for C, as placeholders to be confirmed by the business.

planned_decisions.case: ship_cost: partial kilograms (e.g. 1.2 kg)
planned_decisions.default: Round the weight up to the next whole kilogram before charging.

planned_decisions.case: ship_cost: zone is lower case, has spaces, or is unknown, blank or missing
planned_decisions.default: Trim spaces and ignore letter case, so ' b ' is zone B. An unknown, blank or missing zone returns NULL rather than a guessed price.

planned_decisions.case: ship_cost: weight zero, negative, missing, or over a maximum parcel weight
planned_decisions.default: Zero or negative returns NULL. Missing returns NULL. No maximum weight limit; heavy parcels are priced by the same formula.

planned_decisions.case: slugify: allowed characters, case and separators
planned_decisions.default: Lower case, letters and digits only, with runs of other characters collapsed to a single hyphen and no leading or trailing hyphen.

planned_decisions.case: slugify: accented or non-Latin characters (e.g. Café, 日本)
planned_decisions.default: Accents are transliterated to plain ASCII (Café becomes cafe). Characters with no ASCII equivalent are dropped.

planned_decisions.case: slugify: symbols such as & and apostrophes
planned_decisions.default: Apostrophes are removed without a hyphen (Bob's becomes bobs). '&' is treated as a separator and dropped.

planned_decisions.case: slugify: very long titles, or titles that produce an empty slug (only symbols), or missing/blank titles
planned_decisions.default: No length limit. Empty results and NULL/blank input return an empty string for blank and NULL for NULL.

planned_decisions.case: slugify: two different titles that give the same slug
planned_decisions.default: The function stays pure and returns the same slug. Uniqueness is the caller's job.

planned_decisions.case: avg_stars: rounding of the headline rating
planned_decisions.default: Arithmetic mean rounded to 1 decimal place, half up.

planned_decisions.case: avg_stars: ratings outside 1-5 (0, 6, negative), fractional, or non-numeric
planned_decisions.default: Ignore ratings outside 1 to 5 and non-numeric values. Fractional ratings within the range are kept as given.

planned_decisions.case: avg_stars: NULL ratings, or no valid ratings at all
planned_decisions.default: NULL ratings are ignored and not counted. If no valid ratings remain, return NULL, not 0.

planned_decisions.case: avg_stars: products with very few ratings (one 5-star review)
planned_decisions.default: Show the plain average with no minimum count or Bayesian smoothing.
